newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Varazdinska sees '96 net up at HRK28 mln.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Varazdinska sees '96 net up at HRK28 mln.

text.p: Croatia's Varazdinska Banka, one of the country's top five banks by capital, said on Thursday it expected 1996 net of roughly 28 million kuna, compared to 19 million in 1995.
"Some 9.5 million will be paid out in dividend and the rest passed to reserves to strengthen our total capital," president Mato Lukinic told a news conference.
Varazdinska paid 50 kuna per share dividend on 1995 results.
The bank made some 26 million kuna risk provisions although most of its borrowers are sound. Interest income accounts for some 40 percent of its income, Lukinic said.
The bank will probably lower its lending rates from the current 12-16 percent on average this year. "We have to do it, and not only because of competition," he added.
Varazdinska, which is relatively conservative in its policies, also hopes to boost its loan portfolio and improve the range of services.

This it plans to do with the help of higher deposits, which Lukinic said are rising at a much stronger pace since the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) bought a 10-percent stake in it.
The bank also aims to get some of the $40 million Croatia is negotiating with the World Bank to boost the banking sector, Lukinic said.
